tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/tls-backend.md <<'EOF'
# TLS backend

The project's current recorded decision is to use rustls as the TLS backend, chosen because it is a pure Rust implementation and avoids the CVE exposure the project wanted to leave behind. This was decided by the user on 2026-09-24.
EOF
cat docs/policies/tls-backend.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/tls-backend.md`. It states that the project's current recorded decision is rustls as the TLS backend. The reasons given are that it is a pure Rust implementation and avoids the CVE exposure. It dates the decision to 2026-09-24 and attributes it to the user.

The decision comes from Muninn record #16, which is user-stated (trust 3) and retired the earlier TLS records (#13 and #14). The file doesn't mention the retired alternative. Muninn's `why` check reported the record as sufficient.

The file wasn't created on my first attempt. The shell command failed with a parser error, so I wrote it with the Write tool instead.

Muninn's session context also showed a heartbeat warning: 11 hook runs started and never finished. That may mean a hook is exceeding its timeout. I didn't look into it.
